name: Peptide Mass Calculator
tagline: Monoisotopic mass, m/z for any charge state, and the theoretical isotope envelope of a peptide sequence.
description: Enter a peptide sequence in one-letter code and get its elemental composition, monoisotopic and average mass, m/z values across charge states, and a theoretical isotope distribution you can export as a publication-ready figure. Supports common fixed modifications. Runs entirely in your browser.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.label: Peptide sequence
inputs.help: One-letter amino acid codes (20 standard residues). Whitespace and digits are ignored. Lowercase is accepted. Example: DRVYIHPF (angiotensin II).

inputs.name: maxCharge
inputs.label: Max charge state
inputs.help: m/z is reported for every charge from 1+ up to this value. Tryptic peptides are usually 2+ or 3+; large or basic peptides may reach 5+ or more.

inputs.name: carbamidomethyl
inputs.label: Carbamidomethyl cysteine (+57.021)
inputs.help: Adds C2H3NO to every cysteine. Use when samples were alkylated with iodoacetamide, which is standard in bottom-up proteomics.

inputs.name: cyclic
inputs.label: Cyclic (head-to-tail)
inputs.help: Removes one water (−18.011 Da) to model a head-to-tail cyclic peptide, which has no free N- or C-terminus.

inputs.name: isotopePeaks
inputs.label: Isotope peaks to compute
inputs.help: Number of isotopologue peaks (M, M+1, M+2, ...) shown in the isotope envelope. 8 is enough for peptides under ~3 kDa; use more for larger peptides.

seo.title: Peptide Mass Calculator: monoisotopic mass, m/z, isotopes
seo.metaDescription: Free peptide mass calculator: monoisotopic and average mass, m/z for each charge state, and an exportable isotope distribution. Runs in your browser.

faq.q: What is the difference between monoisotopic and average mass?
faq.a: Monoisotopic mass uses the most abundant isotope of each element (12C, 1H, 14N, 16O, 32S) and matches the first peak of the isotope envelope in high-resolution MS. Average mass weights all isotopes by natural abundance and matches the centroid of the whole envelope.

faq.q: How is m/z calculated from mass?
faq.a: m/z = (M + z × 1.007276) / z, where M is the neutral monoisotopic mass and 1.007276 Da is the proton mass.
